requirement_text.REQ-039: GitHub issue #71 (verified by `gh issue view 71`). Companion (+1) registration through a companion code, with consent before storage and invited_by_user_id attribution. A code with grants_companion_of = X sets registrations.invited_by_user_id = X, one field for both mechanic and referral reporting, no schema change. The companion completes NAME, PHONE, COMPANY only, reusing REQ-030's reduced-field pattern. Consent before storage is the security-critical property -- nothing is written before consent_pd_at is set. Companions occupy a normal seat, waitlisted like anyone else when full. One use unless the organizer overrides max_uses. Both guest and host are notified once each, transactionally; host notification carries name+company only, never phone/email (S3).

task.description: WF-02 Step 2 (Implementation) for REQ-039 on branch feature/WF02-REQ-039 (started at commit 99fdd8c). Implemented exactly the approved, reworked design (docs/agents/design/REQ-039.md, passed re-gate after rework 1). No schema/migration change anywhere (git grep over apps/bot confirms grantsCompanionOf, the pre-existing column, is the only companion-related column touched; no new migration file created; AC2 satisfied by construction). Changes: (1) domain/inviteCode.ts -- redeemInviteCode gains an optional `companionProfile: { name, company, phone } | null = null` parameter (default null, every existing caller unchanged); the locked codeRows SELECT (step 5) gains `grantsCompanionOf`; the registrations insert/update (step 10) gains `invitedByUserId: codeRow.grantsCompanionOf`, unconditional on companionProfile (a no-op for personal/bulk codes, always null there); when companionProfile !== null, a Profile row is written via profile.ts's createWalkinProfile immediately before the registrations write, in the same transaction, with the onConflictDoNothing race backstop. New pure functions (placed here, Open Question 3 resolved in favor of co-locating with the feature they serve, not domain/walkin.ts): parseCompanionFieldsMessage/formatCompanionConfirmMessage/parseCompanionConfirmMessage (the message-text-carrier, mirroring domain/walkin.ts's REQ-030 pattern per the design's own instruction), formatCompanionFieldsPrompt/parseCompanionReplyContext (the reply-to-message carrier for the FIRST collection step, mirroring handlers/feedback.ts's formatFeedbackTextPrompt/parseFeedbackReplyContext precedent -- not explicitly named in the design's own component/type-structure section, since that section only covers Open Question 4's already-flagged wiring gap), and getCompanionDisplayData (structurally excludes profiles.phone/profiles.email from its SELECT clause, S3/S11, mirroring listInviteCodeRedeemers's existing discipline). (2) domain/profile.ts -- createWalkinProfile gains an optional `options: { onConflictDoNothing?: boolean }` parameter, default {} (REQ-030's own call site in domain/walkin.ts is unchanged, byte-for-byte, since it never passes this option); only REQ-039's companion call site passes `{ onConflictDoNothing: true }`. (3) domain/notification.ts -- one new NotificationKind member, 'companion_registered'. (4) handlers/start.ts's resolveInviteDeepLink -- after the unchanged hasConsented gate, two read-only lookups (getInviteCodeByCode, then getProfileByUserId only when the code is a companion code) decide whether to enter the reduced-field collection flow (send the prompt, no write, return) or fall through to the existing unconditional redeemInviteCode call (now also covering a companion code redeemed by a returning guest with an existing Profile row, per the design's Open Question 1 resolution). Both makeStartHandler and makeConsentCallbackHandler gained an optional `sender: NotificationSender | null = null` parameter (default null, so start.test.ts's existing `makeStartHandler(db)`/`makeConsentCallbackHandler(db)` construction calls keep compiling and behaving unchanged) threaded through to resolveInviteDeepLink for the host notification. (5) NEW FILE handlers/companion.ts -- the reply-to-message listener (makeCompanionTextReplyHandler) that catches the guest's free-text 'Name | Company | Phone' reply and renders the confirm message (no write), the confirm-tap callback (makeCompanionConfirmCallbackHandler) that re-parses the confirm message's own text and performs the single combined write via redeemInviteCode, a Cancel callback (makeCompanionCancelCallbackHandler, mirrors handlers/walkin.ts's walkin:cancel), and the shared sendCompanionHostNotification helper used by BOTH this file's confirm callback (a brand-new guest) AND handlers/start.ts's resolveInviteDeepLink (a returning guest redeemed directly) -- see result.issues for the one interpretive completion this required beyond the design's literal text. (6) i18n/types.ts, en.ts, ru.ts -- one new top-level catalog key `companion` (provisional English/Russian copy per decisions/0002, CONTENT-BA owns final wording), including a fixed, non-localized `refLinePrefix` mirrored for catalogs.test.ts's parity check only (same precedent as feedback.refLinePrefix/noShow.refLinePrefix -- never actually read through the catalog at runtime; the real anchor is domain/inviteCode.ts's COMPANION_REF_LINE_PREFIX constant). (7) index.ts -- wires makeStartHandler/makeConsentCallbackHandler with the process-wide notificationSender, and registers the three new companion handlers (confirm callback, cancel callback, the message:text reply listener, registered after every bot.command(...) registration per this file's own established ordering discipline).
acceptance_criteria: A guest redeeming a companion code whose grants_companion_of is host H gets a registration with invited_by_user_id = H's user id and invite_code_id set to that code -- verified by reading the row.
git grep over apps/bot finds no companion-specific column, no referral table and no second attribution field: invited_by_user_id is the only mechanism, and no migration adds another.
Abandoning the companion flow AT OR BEFORE the consent step leaves ZERO new users rows, ZERO new profiles rows and ZERO new registrations rows for that guest.
Completing the flow collects name, phone and company and nothing further.
A companion redeeming against a FULL event is waitlisted, not admitted, and not given a seat outside capacity.
A second person attempting to redeem a single-use companion code is refused and no registration is created.

Both the guest and the host receive exactly one message on a successful companion registration; the host's message contains the guest's name and company and contains NEITHER the guest's phone NOR their email.
The guest's phone appears in NO log line and in NO audit_log payload.
Each companion registration writes exactly one audit_log row.

result.summary: All 9 ACs implemented per the approved design; no schema/migration change (confirmed by `git status` on apps/bot/drizzle and `git diff --stat` on schema.ts showing zero changes). `npm run lint -w apps/bot` -- clean, zero errors/warnings. `npm run build -w apps/bot` (tsc) -- clean, zero errors. `npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism` (run from apps/bot) -- 88 test files, 810 tests, ALL PASSED, 0 failures, run duration ~123s; no rework/re-run needed (ISS-0031's contention-pattern re-run condition did not trigger). REQ-038's own existing tests (redeem.db.test.ts, start.test.ts, and every other suite touching redeemInviteCode/resolveInviteDeepLink/makeStartHandler/makeConsentCallbackHandler) required ZERO edits -- companionProfile defaults to null and sender defaults to null for every pre-existing call site, confirmed by the unmodified test files still passing unchanged. AC-by-AC: AC1 -- redeemInviteCode's registrations write now sets invitedByUserId: codeRow.grantsCompanionOf unconditionally (a no-op for personal/bulk codes, whose grantsCompanionOf is always null per REQ-033/037's issuing functions). AC2 -- git grep -n 'companion' apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts returns exactly one line, the pre-existing grantsCompanionOf column; no new migration file in apps/bot/drizzle/. AC3 -- the reduced-field collection flow (resolveInviteDeepLink's new branch, handlers/companion.ts's text-reply listener and confirm callback) performs no DB write of any kind until the single confirm tap calls redeemInviteCode; the consent gate (unchanged position, first statement of resolveInviteDeepLink) still runs before any of this. AC4 -- parseCompanionFieldsMessage/parseCompanionConfirmMessage together ask exactly Name/Company/Phone, nothing else; no experience/student/links prompt exists anywhere in the new code. AC5 -- companion redemption calls the unchanged redeemInviteCode/decideRegistrationOutcome, so a full event's companion redemption waitlists via the exact same branch a personal/bulk code would (no companion-specific capacity path was added). AC6 -- validateInviteCodeForRedemption's usedCount>=maxUses check is untouched; a companion code's maxUses is set once at issue time (REQ-037, unchanged). AC7 -- the guest's own reply reuses the unchanged composeRegistrationReply; the host is notified exactly once via the new companion_registered NotificationKind through sendLedgeredNotification's existing (registrationId, kind) idempotency; getCompanionDisplayData's SELECT clause structurally excludes profiles.phone and profiles.email (never selected, so they cannot appear in the composed text by construction, not by a runtime filter). AC8 -- no log line or writeAuditLog payload in the changed code ever reads companionProfile.phone/parsed.fields.phone; the audit payload for a companion redemption is the same `{ eventId, inviteCodeId }` shape every other redemption already writes (unchanged). AC9 -- the single writeAuditLog call inside redeemInviteCode's transaction is unchanged/unconditional; the Profile insert (guarded, may no-op) writes no separate audit row either way.
issues: INTERPRETIVE COMPLETION (flagged, not a silent business-rule invention): the design's own §7 AC-map row for AC7 cites only §4 (the confirm-callback path, a brand-new guest) and §6 (the notification mechanism itself) -- it does not explicitly restate, the way it does for AC1 ('holds identically for a returning guest'), that the host notification must also fire on the direct-redemption branch a returning guest (existing Profile row) takes per Open Question 1's resolution. I implemented the host notification for BOTH branches (handlers/companion.ts's sendCompanionHostNotification is called from both the confirm callback and handlers/start.ts's resolveInviteDeepLink), reasoning that AC7's issue text ('Both the guest and the host receive exactly one message on a successful companion registration') states no returning-guest carve-out, and that this only applies the design's own fully-specified §6 mechanism to a symmetric case, not new business logic. REVIEWER/SECURITY-REVIEWER should confirm this reading rather than treat it as settled.

DESIGN GAP, not filled in: the typed /redeem command (handlers/registration.ts's makeRedeemCommandHandler) is outside every version of this design's artifacts_in list and its own §0 table (which names only handlers/start.ts's resolveInviteDeepLink as the modified handler). A companion code redeemed via /redeem therefore still gets full invited_by_user_id attribution (AC1, unconditional on companionProfile) and the one-use/capacity/waitlist rules (AC5/AC6, unchanged shared logic) but does NOT go through the reduced-field collection flow and does NOT trigger a host notification -- it silently falls through to the same companionProfile: null path a returning guest takes. This is left unchanged, per instruction not to invent scope the approved design never analyzed; flagging for ORCH/CODE-DESIGNER to decide whether a follow-up requirement or design amendment is needed.

OPEN (carried from design, unresolved by BACKEND-DEV per instruction not to invent content): Open Questions #4/#5's copy items -- the exact companion.* catalog strings (fieldsPrompt, missingName, missingPhone, confirmStatement, staleMessage, button labels, cancelled, hostNotification) are provisional/placeholder English+Russian text, matching every prior invite-code requirement's own precedent (decisions/0002, CONTENT-BA owns final wording). The 'Event:' line in formatCompanionConfirmMessage/formatCompanionCanonicalLines is included per the design's own stated assumption (Open Question #5, 'the design assumes yes').

next_action: Route to REVIEWER (Step 2b) for design-system/code-quality/scope review, per WF-02's standard sequencing; SECURITY-REVIEWER gate follows per core-directives.md (this change touches personal data, consent, and a new notification kind).
